title_zh: 丁俊晖：让斯诺克在中国流行起来的球员
title_en: Famous Chinese People (12/20): Ding Junhui, the Player Who Made Snooker Popular in China
note_en: 为了 (wèile) "in order to" introduces a goal, and in Chinese the goal comes first, before the main action: 为了专心练习，他很早就离开学校 "To focus on practice, he left school very early." English can put "in order to" at either end of the sentence, but a 为了 phrase normally opens the sentence. The opposite order uses 来 or 以 instead: 卖掉了家里的房子和小商店来支持他 "sold the family's house and small shop (in order) to support him."
